title: the summit sit
hook: a lotus leaf sits in the pond all day, and the water rolls off it in beads
carry: water sliding from a lotus leaf

segments.voice: Yesterday the summit sit went back to the modern teachers, and Ramana's question: to whom did this thought come? Did a worry get asked that question? Today, the three tracks. Day one thousand fifty-one.

Rain falls on a pond. The water gathers on a lotus leaf in bright beads, rolls to the edge, and slides off. The leaf has been in the water all its life. It isn't wet. The Bhagavad Gita uses that leaf in its fifth chapter, as a picture of a person who acts fully in the world and isn't stained by it. That chapter sat inside the lineage weeks of this year, when the path split into three tracks: karma, bhakti and jnana. Today's summit sit climbs back to those weeks.
screen: `WATER ON A LOTUS LEAF.` → `IN THE POND, NOT WET.` → `THE THREE TRACKS.`

segments.voice: Here is the Gita's line, in paraphrase, from chapter five: one who acts while placing every action in Brahman, letting go of clinging, is not touched by wrong, as a lotus leaf is not touched by water. Hold that leaf up and look at it from each of the year's three tracks. On the karma track, we read Gita chapters three, four and five, and designed a year of service. There the leaf means doing the work well and setting down the result. Act, and don't grip the outcome. On the bhakti track, we read the Gita Govinda and the Bhagavata's tenth book, and sang kirtan. There the leaf turns into an offering. Elsewhere the Gita has Krishna say, in paraphrase: whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you give, do it as an offering to me. The act is the same. Now it is a gift. On the jnana track, we read Shankara's Crest-Jewel of Discrimination and the Ashtavakra Gita. There the leaf is the witness. Ashtavakra tells King Janaka, in paraphrase: you are not the earth, not water, not fire, not air, not space; know yourself as the witness of all these. The water rolls by; the one who sees it was never wet. Three tracks, three readings of one leaf. And the Gita itself, in the same chapter, says that only the childish call the path of knowledge and the path of action different; the one who truly stands in either reaches the fruit of both. Read that way, the tracks aren't a contest. They're three ways up.
screen: `NOT TOUCHED, LIKE A LOTUS LEAF.` · `KARMA: SET DOWN THE RESULT.` · `BHAKTI: MAKE IT AN OFFERING.` · `JNANA: THE WITNESS, NEVER WET.` · then, large: `THREE WAYS UP.`

segments.voice: Sit for the bell's two minutes, and bring to mind one ordinary task from today: a dish, an email, a drive. Hold it for a few breaths the karma way: do it well, and let the result go. Then the bhakti way: if you pray, see it as something offered. Then the jnana way: notice the one who watches the task being done, still and dry, like the leaf. Don't pick a favorite. Let each one have a few breaths. The bell holds the time.
Padma-patra. The lotus leaf, sitting in water all its life and never wet, the Gita's picture for the three tracks of karma, bhakti and jnana.
Your line: water sliding from a lotus leaf. Today, finish one task and then lift your hands off it for a moment, like water sliding from a lotus leaf. Day one thousand fifty-one.

howItsDone: The paths of karma, bhakti and jnana are walked side by side and in combination: selfless work and service, devotion in worship and kirtan, and study and inquiry with a teacher; the Gita is read as holding all three.

myth: the Gita says the lotus leaf stays dry because it stays out of the pond
the leaf lives in the water and still isn't touched by it: acting in the world, unstained.
in the Gita's fifth chapter, knowledge and action are called one by the wise
it says only the childish speak of them as different.

he tells him he is none of these, but the witness of them all.

fork.setup: you've finished a piece of work and done it well. the result is out of your hands. what does the Gita's lotus leaf picture suggest?
options: hold on tight until the result comes in.
act fully, then let the result roll off, like water on a leaf.
next time, don't act at all.
fork.reveal: the Gita pictures someone who acts, places the action in Brahman and lets go of clinging, untouched as a lotus leaf by water. it never says to stop acting.

original.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: padma-patra, lotus leaf, the Gita's picture in chapter five.

trapdoor: what you thought: karma, bhakti and jnana are three rival paths.
what it means: the year's three tracks read the same Gita, and the Gita says the wise see knowledge and action as one.
what a scholar hears: Gita 5.4–5 and 5.10, padmapatram ivambhasa, like a lotus leaf by water.
recall: a still gaze at a small mark

notes: Fifth summit sit (1047–1053): revisits the lineage track (964–1005): karma (Gita 3–5, a year of service), bhakti (Gita Govinda, Bhagavata 10, kirtan), jnana (Vivekachudamani, Ashtavakra Gita). 'Crest-Jewel of Discrimination' is used for Vivekachudamani; confirm the English title.

Paraphrases: Gita 5.10 (brahmany adhaya karmani sangam tyaktva karoti yah, lipyate na sa papena padmapatram ivambhasa); 9.27 (whatever you do, eat, offer, give, do it as an offering to me); 5.4–5 (only children, not the wise, speak of Samkhya and Yoga as different). Note Gita 5.2 also says karma yoga excels renunciation of action; the script doesn't raise that, to keep to 5.4–5. Check.
Ashtavakra Gita 1.3 paraphrase (you are not earth, water, fire, air or space; know yourself as the witness of these, as consciousness). Confirm verse number.
Arnold's Song Celestial (1885) is on the validator list, but the writer isn't certain of its exact wording for these verses, so nothing is quoted.
Editor pass: 'the tracks were never meant as a contest' (a claim about intent) softened to 'read that way, the tracks aren't a contest'.
Audit 2026-10-01: checked Gita 5.4, 5.10, 9.27 and Ashtavakra Gita 1.3 paraphrases; no change.
